sources.access: Same URL as INAH-MHI-I-09-00419; alias candidate, not automatically merged

findings.assertion: The Hospital de Jesús foundation date is not uniform across institutional and historical accounts: INAH catalogue 1524; UNAM scholarly synthesis 1521–1524; reproduced older stone inscription circa 1527.
findings.limitations: Founding dates may refer to establishment, building work or later commemorative inscription; original charter unexamined

findings.assertion: The hospital was initially known as Nuestra Señora de la Limpia y Purísima Concepción, later also called Hospital del Marqués after Cortés received the Marquesado del Valle de Oaxaca.
findings.limitations: Later names and dating require comparison with original records

findings.assertion: The Hospital de Jesús retains its hospital function and the UNAM account identifies surviving sixteenth-century staircase and cloisters despite subsequent alterations.
findings.limitations: Current visitor access to interiors not checked

findings.assertion: INAH locates Hospital de Jesús at 20 de Noviembre 82, at Mesones, and records substantial twentieth-century alteration of the street facade.
INAH dates the start of the adjacent Jesús Nazareno temple work to circa 1577 under Claudio de Arciniega, with Alonso Pérez de Castañeda continuing work after 1593.
findings.limitations: Do not conflate temple phases with 1520s hospital foundation

findings.assertion: The UNAM architectural chronology reproduces a 1524 cabildo reference to the hospital as an existing institution, in a land-boundary description for Hernando de Salazar, but the original council folio has not been examined.
findings.limitations: Cannot establish exact foundation date or validate quotation against council manuscript.

findings.assertion: The same UNAM chronology records a 1528 foundation date attributed to Sigüenza y Góngora, and two papal privileges dated 15 and 16 April 1529; these are distinct chronological claims that should not be merged into a single foundation date.
findings.limitations: Papal bulls and Sigüenza original not examined; attribution requires verification.

findings.assertion: The Archivo General de la Nación identifies the Hospital de Jesús fonds as covering 1520–1925, including a 1520 legal power issued by Cortés; the earliest fonds document is not itself proof the hospital operated in 1520.
findings.limitations: No archival item examined; fonds includes Marquesado del Valle materials.

findings.assertion: AGN states that the Hospital de Jesús documents remained at the hospital until 1929, when federal authorities declared the papers national property; the fonds includes pharmacy inventories, patient reports and hospital administration contracts.

A 2023 Mexico City historical publication states the adjacent Jesús Nazareno church was begun by a grandson of Cortés and restarted in 1601, when only some walls and main-chapel vaulting were erected.
findings.limitations: Building contracts and original construction accounts not examined.

findings.assertion: The principal eastern infirmary of Hospital de Jesús was completed in 1535 according to the INAH monument catalogue; the original ward itself should not be presented as a preserved visitor-visible room.
findings.locator: Información histórica, completion of the eastern infirmary
findings.limitations: Original contracts and archaeology not checked

findings.assertion: INAH credits Claudio de Arciniega with the hospital's principal portal, patios and arcades built 1579–1587 alongside the infirmary; surviving courtyard features require phase-by-phase differentiation after later rebuilding.
findings.limitations: Catalogue has a validation warning and original building records uninspected

findings.assertion: INAH records that an Indigenous woman named Petronila Jerónima donated an image of Jesús Nazareno in 1663, after which the hospital used that religious dedication; this is a named Indigenous actor in institutional history.
findings.limitations: Single catalog account, original donation document unexamined

findings.assertion: INAH describes hospital repairs for differential subsidence in 1770 and 1787, followed by arcades replaced by architect Antonio Velázquez after the 1800 earthquake; current arches should not be automatically dated to the sixteenth century.
findings.limitations: Original repair accounts and structural study not checked

findings.assertion: According to INAH, José Villagrán designed a five-story hospital building during the opening of Avenida 20 de Noviembre around 1934, accounting for much of the present street-facing modern appearance.
findings.limitations: INAH catalogue pending validation; design drawings not examined

findings.assertion: INAH reports that widening José María Pino Suárez in 1963 caused the demolition of the hospital's chapel and earliest infirmary built in 1535; any field guide must distinguish this lost fabric from surviving elements.
findings.limitations: INAH catalogue pending validation; demolition plans unexamined
